title: Recent advances in first-row transition metal clusters for photocatalytic water splitting
claim: Combining molecular clusters with light-absorbing semiconductors or porous supports can separate light harvesting from catalytic functions and improve interfacial charge handling.
explanation: The review surveys a BiVO4–reduced-graphene-oxide/cobalt-cubane oxidation composite, titanium-oxo-cluster/CdS/MIL-101 hydrogen-evolution assemblies, lanthanide–nickel clusters on CdS, and POMs immobilized in MOFs.
scope: Cluster-based composite photocatalysts for water oxidation or hydrogen evolution.
conditions: The components must be interfaced appropriately for charge transfer under the reported illumination and reaction conditions.
caveats: Reported performance gains and proposed electron-transfer pathways are system-specific; a composite architecture alone does not guarantee improvement.
